name: RMS Translate
author: RMS Digital Services

sections.description:
Configure languages under Settings > RMS Translate and edit translations in the post editor. Translated content stays in a separate SQLite database. The original language does not open that database on an ordinary front-end request.

Includes translated content, SEO metadata, language links, hreflang, a language switcher and display of saved WooCommerce/builder content. Existing machine-created translations remain readable, exportable and manually editable. This edition has no model calls, provider secrets, AI queue, license client or external installer.

WP-CLI: wp rms-translate status, wp rms-translate export --user=ADMIN, and wp rms-translate set POST_ID LOCALE FIELD --value-file=/local/translation.txt --user=EDITOR.

The pdo_sqlite extension is required. Back up the SQLite store using an online SQLite backup, not a raw copy while WAL writers are active. The plugin registers owner callbacks for compatible RMS Backup installations. For the first update introducing restore leases, finish existing PHP requests before restoring data. Local OS flock is required; shared network filesystem locking is not certified.

No external service is contacted by this edition. No visitor tracking is included. Removing the plugin preserves translations and settings. Configure web-server protection when storage must be inside the web root.

Use only one RMS Translate edition at a time. Keep a backup before switching editions.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate RMS Translate.
  2. Open Settings > RMS Translate, configure language codes, and save.
  3. Edit a post and fill its Translations fields.

short_description: Manual translations in SQLite without cloned WordPress posts or external translation services.
